currentContext.strategies: Focus on value-added services in the automotive segment - financing, maintenance and warranties - to keep luxury vehicle ownership accessible to a broader base of consumers and cushion tighter financing conditions and rising costs|Grow the FineCars footprint in the organised, certified pre-owned luxury segment, expanding inventory and customer base and reaching beyond the major metros into tier-1 and tier-2 cities through local dealers and online platforms|Deepen software-division capabilities in AI-embedded and cloud-native solutions so enterprise clients can modernise legacy systems and improve operational efficiency|Embed digital tools, data analytics and automation inside FTL's own automotive retail operations - inventory management, customer engagement and after-sales servicing - a dual focus on external technology offerings plus internal digital capability|Diversify into electric vehicles via a continued strategic partnership with an EV manufacturer, aligning with the industry transition towards sustainability|Prioritise cost-effective, high-impact solutions for technology clients where IT spending is cautious, particularly in Europe|Ongoing focus on operational excellence, innovation and strategic partnerships, with emphasis on superior customer experience and sustainability
currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no capex project, plant, capacity addition or rupee capital-expenditure plan for FTL. Expansion is described only qualitatively and at the level of footprint and business scope: management says the certified pre-owned luxury segment's growth creates a durable opportunity for FTL's FineCars division to grow its footprint, and that the pre-owned luxury market is expanding reach beyond major metros into tier-1 and tier-2 cities through local dealers and online platforms, giving FineCars scope to enhance its inventory and customer base. The after-sales car industry is described as supporting the continued expansion of authorised service centres and creating additional recurring revenue streams for the Company, though no specific centre, location or timeline is named. On the corporate side, the Board approved on 8th January 2026 the shifting of the Registered Office within Delhi to the 5th Floor, Eros Corporate Tower, Nehru Place, effective the same date, and on 30th March 2026 approved altering the Main Objects clause of the Memorandum of Association by adding new clauses 3 to 8 with a view to expanding the business activities of the Company - approved by Members through a Special Resolution dated 29th April 2026 by postal ballot. Diversification into electric vehicles is pursued through a continued strategic partnership with an EV manufacturer rather than through own capacity. The Company states it has not taken any major step to conserve energy, and there were no foreign exchange earnings or outgo during the year.

risks.risk: Structural shift of India's automobile industry towards electric mobility and changing consumer preferences
risks.note: Management lists this as a threat that may impact traditional luxury vehicle sales and services - FTL's core business is the retail of pre-owned luxury cars, so a technology shift in the underlying vehicle parc erodes the value and saleability of its inventory and service proposition. The Company's stated mitigation is a continued strategic partnership with an EV manufacturer.

risks.risk: Near-term softness in new luxury vehicle sales driven by currency volatility and tariff-related price increases
risks.note: The AR notes F.Y. 2025-26 was marked by moderation in growth after a period of strong expansion, with currency volatility, tariff actions and price increases moderating demand growth even as luxury vehicle sales reached a record of approximately 55,000-56,000 units in calendar year 2025. Weakness in new-car sales feeds through to the pre-owned market FTL depends on.

risks.risk: Elevated global energy prices arising from ongoing geopolitical conflict
risks.note: Flagged as capable of raising operating costs across the sector; separately, management says elevated energy costs may increase input and logistics costs for the automotive trade and dampen demand for high-value assets like luxury vehicles. The AR attributes this to the Middle East conflict that commenced in early 2026 and disrupted energy supply routes including the Strait of Hormuz.

risks.risk: Persistent industry-wide shortage of EV-certified service technicians
risks.note: Explicitly flagged as a threat that could raise operating costs and affect after-sales service quality across the sector - directly relevant because after-sales servicing is described as a critical, recurring revenue segment for the Company.

risks.risk: Cautious IT spending in developed markets, particularly Europe
risks.note: Management says elevated energy costs and cautious IT spending in certain developed markets, particularly Europe, may require FTL to continue prioritising cost-effective, high-impact solutions for its clients - a demand and pricing constraint on the technology services division.

risks.risk: Consumer-sentiment and financing sensitivity of high-value discretionary purchases
risks.note: Cautious consumer sentiment stemming from the global conflict could dampen demand for high-value assets like luxury vehicles; the Company relies on value-added services such as financing, maintenance and warranties to cushion the impact of tighter financing conditions and rising costs.

risks.risk: Market, currency and commodity price volatility, supply chain disruption, technological disruption and regulatory compliance
risks.note: The MD&A Risks and Concerns section names these as the risk categories the Board-approved risk management framework is designed to manage, with oversight by the Risk Management Committee together with the Audit Committee and half-yearly 'Risks that Matter' reporting.

risks.risk: Rising competitive intensity in both the organised pre-owned luxury car market and IT services
risks.note: The Future Outlook describes an increasingly competitive and dynamic environment; the addressable market is widening through digital retail adoption and tier-1/tier-2 penetration, which attracts organised competitors, while global IT spending remains cautious.
